claims.claim: **Alkalis include** drain and oven cleaners, automatic dishwashing liquids and powders, laundry detergents, ammonia and Portland cement.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Significant GI ulceration is likely once the pH is above 11.5.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get the container** to check contents and strength. Corrosive potential varies with concentration and preparation: **liquids are more likely than powders to burn the oesophagus.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check the product with the Poisons Information Centre** to establish whether it is weak, strong, irritant or corrosive.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Exposure can severely burn the GI tract, especially the oesophagus.** **No mouth or pharyngeal ulcers does not rule out gastro-oesophageal lesions.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms may be minimal:** pain · nausea and vomiting · drooling, or refusal of food and drink · ⚠️ stridor or respiratory distress.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic: fluid dilution with water 10 mL/kg, max 250 mL.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** once 4 hours have passed with no symptoms and the child can eat and drink.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any symptoms: contact the surgical registrar and admit for oesophagoscopy.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Alkalis poisoning' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Alkalis_poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
